<SinceRelease version="2.2.0" product="tsdb" />

{C.SKIPSCAN_LONG} dramatically speeds up `DISTINCT` queries. It jumps directly to the first row of each distinct value in an
index instead of scanning all rows. First introduced for the rowstore hypertables and relational tables,
{C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} now extends to columnstore hypertables, distinct aggregates like `COUNT(DISTINCT)`, and even multiple columns.

## Speed up `DISTINCT` queries

You use `DISTINCT` queries to get only the unique values in your data. For example, the IDs of customers who placed orders, the countries where your users are located, or the devices reporting into an IoT system. You might also have graphs and alarms that repeatedly query the most recent values for every device or service.

As your tables get larger, `DISTINCT` queries tend to get slower. Even when your index matches
the exact order and columns for these kinds of queries, {C.PG} (without {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT}) has to scan the
entire index and then run deduplication. As the table grows, this operation keeps
getting slower.

{C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} is an optimization for `DISTINCT` and `DISTINCT ON` queries, including multi-column `DISTINCT`. {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} allows queries to incrementally jump from one ordered value to the next,
without reading the rows in between. Conceptually, {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} is a regular IndexScan that skips across an
index looking for the next value that is greater than the current value.

When you issue a query that uses {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT}, the `EXPLAIN` output includes a new `Custom Scan (SkipScan)`
operator, or node, that can quickly return distinct items from a properly
ordered index. As it locates one item, the {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} node quickly restarts the search for
the next item. This is a much more efficient way of finding distinct items in an
ordered index.

{C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} cost is based on the ratio of distinct tuples to total tuples. If the number of distinct tuples is close to the total number of tuples, {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} is unlikely to be used due to its higher estimated cost.

Multi-column {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} is supported for queries that do not produce NULL distinct values. For example:

```sql
CREATE INDEX ON metrics(region, device, metric_type, time DESC);
-- All distinct columns have filters which don't allow NULLs: can use SkipScan
SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device, metric_type) *
FROM   metrics
WHERE region IN ('UK','EU','JP') AND device > 1 AND metric_type IS NOT NULL
ORDER  BY region, device, metric_type, time DESC;
-- Distinct columns are declared NOT NULL: can use SkipScan with an index on (region, device, time DESC)
CREATE TABLE metrics(region TEXT NOT NULL, device INT NOT NULL, ...);
SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device) *
FROM   metrics
ORDER  BY region, device, time DESC;
```

For benchmarking information on how {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} compares to regular `DISTINCT`
queries, see the [SkipScan blog post](https://www.tigerdata.com/blog/skipscan-in-timescaledb-why-distinct-was-slow-how-we-built-it-and-how-you-can-use-it).

## Use {C.SKIPSCAN_SHORT} queries

Design your layout:

- Rowstore: create an index starting with the `DISTINCT` columns, followed by your time sort. If the `DISTINCT` columns are not the first in your index, ensure any leading columns are used as constraints in your query. This means that if you are asking a question such as "retrieve a list of unique IDs in order" and "retrieve the last reading of each ID," you need at least one index like this:

    ```sql
    CREATE INDEX "cpu_customer_tags_id_time_idx"
    ON readings (customer_id, tags_id, time DESC)
    ```

- Columnstore: set `tsdb.segmentby` to the distinct columns and `tsdb.orderby` to match your query's sort. Convert your historical chunks to the columnstore.

With your index set up correctly, you should start to see immediate benefit for
`DISTINCT` queries. When SkipScan is chosen for your query, the `EXPLAIN
ANALYZE` output shows one or more `Custom Scan (SkipScan)` nodes, like this:

```sql
->  Unique
  ->  Merge Append
        Sort Key: readings.customer_id, readings.tags_id
        ->  Custom Scan (SkipScan) on _hyper_8_79_chunk
              ->  Index Only Scan using _hyper_8_79_chunk_cpu_customer_tags_id_time_idx on _hyper_8_79_chunk
                    Index Cond: ((customer_id > NULL::integer) AND (tags_id > NULL::integer))
        ->  Custom Scan (SkipScan) on _hyper_8_80_chunk
              ->  Index Only Scan using _hyper_8_80_chunk_cpu_customer_tags_id_time_idx on _hyper_8_80_chunk
                    Index Cond: ((customer_id > NULL::integer) AND (tags_id > NULL::integer))
```

<TestPlan>
target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
4. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE metrics (time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, region TEXT, device INT, metric_type TEXT, value DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable);`
5. run SQL: `INSERT INTO metrics SELECT '2026-01-01'::timestamptz + i * INTERVAL '10 seconds', (ARRAY['UK', 'EU', 'JP', 'US'])[1 + i % 4], 1 + i % 20, (ARRAY['cpu', 'mem', 'disk'])[1 + i % 3], random() FROM generate_series(1, 200000) AS i;`
6. run SQL: `CREATE INDEX ON metrics(region, device, metric_type, time DESC);`
7. run SQL: `ANALYZE metrics;`
8. run SQL: `SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device, metric_type) * FROM metrics WHERE region IN ('UK','EU','JP') AND device > 1 AND metric_type IS NOT NULL ORDER BY region, device, metric_type, time DESC;`
9. run SQL: `CREATE FUNCTION plan_lines(query TEXT) RETURNS SETOF TEXT LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN RETURN QUERY EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) ' || query; END $f$;`
10. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device, metric_type) * FROM metrics WHERE region IN ('UK','EU','JP') AND device > 1 AND metric_type IS NOT NULL ORDER BY region, device, metric_type, time DESC$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Custom Scan (SkipScan)%'`
11. run SQL: `DROP TABLE metrics;`
12. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE metrics(region TEXT NOT NULL, device INT NOT NULL, metric_type TEXT, time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, value DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable);`
13. run SQL: `INSERT INTO metrics SELECT (ARRAY['UK', 'EU', 'JP', 'US'])[1 + i % 4], 1 + i % 20, (ARRAY['cpu', 'mem', 'disk'])[1 + i % 3], '2026-01-01'::timestamptz + i * INTERVAL '10 seconds', random() FROM generate_series(1, 200000) AS i;`
14. run SQL: `CREATE INDEX metrics_region_device_time_idx ON metrics USING btree (region, device, time DESC) INCLUDE (value);`
15. run SQL: `ANALYZE metrics;`
16. run SQL: `SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device) * FROM metrics ORDER BY region, device, time DESC;`
17. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT ON (region, device) * FROM metrics ORDER BY region, device, time DESC$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Custom Scan (SkipScan)%'`
18. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE readings (time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, tags_id INT NOT NULL, cpu DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.segmentby = 'customer_id, tags_id', tsdb.orderby = 'time DESC');`
19. run SQL: `INSERT INTO readings SELECT '2026-01-01'::timestamptz + i * INTERVAL '10 seconds', 1 + i % 5, 1 + i % 50, random() FROM generate_series(1, 200000) AS i;`
20. run SQL: `CREATE INDEX "cpu_customer_tags_id_time_idx" ON readings (customer_id, tags_id, time DESC);`
21. run SQL: `ANALYZE readings;`
22. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, tags_id FROM readings ORDER BY customer_id, tags_id$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Custom Scan (SkipScan)%'`
23. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, tags_id FROM readings ORDER BY customer_id, tags_id$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Index Only Scan using %cpu_customer_tags_id_time_idx%'`
24. run SQL: `DO $$ DECLARE chunk regclass; BEGIN FOR chunk IN SELECT show_chunks('readings') LOOP CALL convert_to_columnstore(chunk); END LOOP; END $$;`
25. expect no rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.chunks WHERE hypertable_name = 'readings' AND NOT is_compressed`
26. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, tags_id FROM readings ORDER BY customer_id, tags_id$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Custom Scan (SkipScan)%'`
27. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM plan_lines($q$SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, tags_id FROM readings ORDER BY customer_id, tags_id$q$) AS line WHERE line LIKE '%Custom Scan (ColumnarScan)%'`
